title: Local immutable review packets: Phase 1 design review
subtitle: Representative fixture exercising every report/v1 component. Measurements and evidence files are illustrative fixture data, not claims about any real system.

metadata.reviewRequest: Architecture review and two open decisions

text: Adopt content-addressed packets with separate alias records. Identity is stable across machines in the fixture runs

sections.title: Findings
sections.lede: Each finding states one claim and links the evidence that supports it. Severity ranks impact; the confidence label says how well the claim is established.

blocks.title: Stable asset paths serve stale bytes after an alias change
blocks.claim: When a stylesheet is served from a stable path with a long cache lifetime, switching the alias to a new packet can leave the browser rendering the new HTML with the old stylesheet.

blocks.title: Identity does not depend on machine, clock, or environment
blocks.claim: Three builds from different directories, time zones, and environment orderings produced byte-identical inventories and the same content ID.

blocks.title: Physical-device Safari behavior is not yet established
blocks.claim: Engine-level WebKit runs are not a physical iPad. Touch scrolling of wide tables and code needs a device check before this is called proven.

blocks.title: Authored text is escaped, never interpreted
claim: render as visible text. There is no raw HTML field in report/v1.

blocks.title: Build, verify, publish, alias
blocks.caption: Aliases are the only mutable step. Verification gates publication and runs again on read-back.

steps.label: report/v1 source
steps.detail: Structured JSON plus evidence files; no templates.

steps.label: Deterministic build
steps.detail: index.html, fingerprinted assets and evidence, manifest, checksums.

steps.label: Verify
steps.detail: Recompute every digest and the content ID; never repair.

steps.label: Publish
steps.detail: Stage, verify, rename to packets/<content-id>/; read back.

steps.label: Alias
steps.detail: Compare-and-swap aliases/<name>.json to the new content ID.

blocks.title: src/packet/build.mjs — content ID derivation
blocks.caption: Highlighted lines are the identity boundary: only the canonical manifest without its own ID is hashed.

blocks.title: server: alias responses become non-cacheable redirects
blocks.caption: Before the change, the alias path served packet bytes directly with the packet's long cache lifetime.

blocks.title: Verify and publish from a shell
blocks.source:
# Build, verify, and publish; each step exits non-zero on any mismatch.
canon build fixtures/report/phase1-review.report.json --out dist/packet --receipt dist/build-receipt.json
canon verify dist/packet && canon publish dist/packet --root dist/store --build-receipt dist/build-receipt.json
canon alias set review "$CONTENT_ID" --root dist/store --expect-generation 0

sections.title: Decisions
sections.lede: What needs a decision, the recommendation, and the alternatives considered.

blocks.question: Should packets ever include first-party JavaScript?
blocks.recommendation: No for Phase 1. Every reading feature works without script, and a script-src 'none' policy is simpler to verify.

alternatives.label: No script
alternatives.summary: Strictest CSP; copy-to-clipboard and theme toggles are omitted.

alternatives.label: Hashed first-party script
alternatives.summary: Allows small enhancements; requires hash-based CSP and a script review for every change.

blocks.question: How are concurrent alias updates resolved?
blocks.recommendation: Compare-and-swap on the alias generation under an exclusive lock file; a stale expectation fails rather than overwriting.

alternatives.label: Last writer wins
alternatives.summary: Simple, but silently discards a concurrent update.

alternatives.label: Compare-and-swap
alternatives.summary: Callers state the generation they expect; mismatches fail loudly.

blocks.title: Crashed alias writer leaves a lock file
blocks.mitigation: Updates fail closed with an explicit alias-locked error; the operator removes the lock after confirming no writer is running.

blocks.title: Evidence contains sensitive material
mitigation: Evidence is copied only when declared as a file; withheld items are listed as redacted or unavailable

items: Evidence: 32 files, 4 MiB each, 16 MiB total; text/plain, text/csv, application/json only.
Code: 200 KiB and 4,000 lines per block, 1 MiB total.
